hypotheses: nu > 0 is an arbitrary positive viscosity (the theorem is asserted for every nu > 0).
preamble_entries.conclusion: There exist a force f in C_c^inf(R^3 x (0,inf); R^3), a compact set K subset R^3, and smooth velocity and pressure fields u, p on R^3 x [0,1) satisfying the Navier-Stokes system (1.1): d_t u + (u.grad)u - nu Lap u + grad p = f, div u = 0, u(.,0) = 0, such that supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) subset K for every 0 <= t < 1, sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L2(R^3)} < inf, and limsup_{t->1} ||u(t)||_{L^inf(R^3)} = inf. Consequently there is no smooth solution (u,P) on R^3 x [0,inf) with the same force and initial datum whose kinetic energy sup_{t>=0} (1/2) int |u|^2 dx is uniformly bounded.
constants: nu > 0 arbitrary; singular time t = 1
force support: compact in space (K) and in time (0,inf); the outline (p.16) supports f in K x [0,2] and vanishing on [0, 1 - tau_0] with 0 < tau_0 < 1/2
viscosity rescaling u_nu(x,t) = sqrt(nu) u(x/sqrt(nu), t), p_nu = nu p(x/sqrt(nu), t), f_nu = sqrt(nu) f(x/sqrt(nu), t) (p.7)
core energy scale E_core ~ tau^{1/2-3h}, dissipation D_core ~ tau^{-1/2-3h}, integrable since h < 1/6 (p.16)
preamble_entries.role: Main theorem: finite-time L^inf blowup with bounded energy and smooth compactly supported force, establishing alternative (C) of the Millennium problem statement; the local construction is Theorem 3.1 and the localization/uniqueness steps are in Section 10.

hypotheses: No external hypotheses: an existence statement. It asserts constants 0 < h < 1/100, q_* > 0, 0 < X_a < X_ext < inf and smooth fields (u,p) on Omega_* = {(x,t): tau > 0, q < q_*}, with tau = 1 - t and q = q(z,tau) the concentration scale determined by tau = q(1 - eta^2), z = q^D eta (3.2).
preamble_entries.conclusion: (i) There is a vector potential A and an axisymmetric scalar B with u = curl A + B e_theta (3.3); A and B e_theta are smooth in Cartesian coordinates at the axis and u is exactly divergence-free. (ii) Every Cartesian space-time derivative of A, B e_theta, p is uniformly bounded on compact spatial subsets with c <= q <= c' < q_* (each 0 < c < c') up to the one-sided boundary tau = 0, with limits compatible under differentiation. (iii) For every alpha, b, N and finite X_1: |d_x^alpha d_t^b R(u,p)| <= C_{alpha,b,N,X_1} q^N for 0 <= X <= X_1 as q -> 0 (3.4); for X >= X_ext the residual is identically zero and A = 0, B = K(r,tau), p = -int_r^inf K(rho,tau)^2/rho d rho, K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2) (3.5), where H_ext is smooth on [0,inf) with each fixed derivative bounded and K satisfies the radial swirl heat equation -d_tau K = d_r^2 K + r^{-1} d_r K - r^{-2} K. (iv) For some fixed X_in in (0,X_a) and e_0 > 0: u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau), 0, 0, 1 - tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0 + O(tau^{2h})) as tau -> 0 (3.6).

preamble_entries.role: States the completed local construction (summed corrections before localization): potential representation, boundedness away from the origin up to t = 1, flat residual near the origin, exact heat exterior, and leading velocity growth; it is the input to the localization in Section 10 and Theorem 1.1.

hypotheses: A leading field (velocity and pressure) is given; alternatively a scalar auxiliary profile in the similarity variables (X, eta) is given.
preamble_entries.conclusion: A leading field is regular at the axis if its velocity and pressure extend smoothly across r = 0 in Cartesian coordinates for t < 1. For scalar auxiliary profiles, regular at the axis means a smooth extension in (X, eta) to X = 0.
preamble_entries.role: Fixes the meaning of axis regularity used throughout the profile construction (e.g. the analytic axis profile of Proposition B.2 and the hypotheses of Lemma A.8 and Proposition A.10).

hypotheses: alpha >= 0 and beta > 0 are parameters or expressions depending on profile variables.
preamble_entries.conclusion: One writes alpha << beta when alpha/beta is required to be sufficiently small, with the allowed size depending on all data already fixed. In a chain of constants, choices proceed from right to left; small reciprocals specify large parameters. For expressions depending on profile variables the smallness is uniform on the stated domain and is ensured by those parameter choices.
preamble_entries.role: Fixes the convention for the parameter ordering used in the appendices, in particular the chain (A.6) for the outer profile and the order of choices (B.40) for the axis and joining.

hypotheses: alpha_1, ..., alpha_m are distinct real numbers.
For each j, beta_j is a nonnegative, nonzero smooth function supported in the interior of a compact interval I_j subset (0, inf), with the intervals ordered I_1 < ... < I_m.
For the last assertion: the data vary smoothly over a compact parameter set and the stated separations (distinct exponents, ordered supports) persist.
entries.conclusion: The matrix B_ij = int_0^inf x^{alpha_i} beta_j(x) dx is invertible. The assertion also holds for exponential weights in a logarithmic coordinate. If the data vary smoothly over a compact parameter set and the separations persist, the inverse B^{-1} and each fixed parameter derivative of it are bounded. (The proof notes this does not give a uniform inverse when two exponents approach one another.)
